items.quote: the king had put the officer on whose arm he leaned in charge of the gate, and the people trampled him in the gateway, and he died
items.contrast: The officer was trampled; the king was the person who had assigned him to the gate.
items.reason: The reader must resolve “him” as referring to the officer rather than the nearby king. The sentence’s structure keeps the officer as the person at the gate who was trampled and died.
